producer_report.summary:
I added the newcomer gate as a tested library function in the study crate. It is not wired into any publish step, so nothing blocks a real explainer yet. The root cause is that verification checked the study's rules but never asked a newcomer whether the page is useful. A fresh model reader with no tools now reads only the rendered page and rates it 1 to 5 against its own prompt (`prompts/newcomer.md`).

`MIN_NEWCOMER_SCORE` is 4, and a score below it is a `Rejection` whose findings are the reader's reasons. These cases also block:
- Missing or malformed output: no structured output, a score outside 1–5 or not an integer, or no reasons.
- A reader that fails, is killed, or hits a driver error.

Only `Ok(Rating)` ships.

The structural checks on the intro and glossary run first, and the reader is not called if one fails. Each has a documented reason and names its criterion and the offending text:
- intro present
- glossary terms defined
- backticked terms defined in the glossary
- no raw ids like `c12`
- size limits

The reader runs through `AgentDriver`. `rate_page` overwrites the prompts, tools and schema of whatever invocation template it is given, so no producer or verifier material reaches the reader.

`docs/design/explainer-site.md` records the gate, the three alternatives and why the independent reader was chosen. It also states the limits: one noisy model judgment, and a fresh reader that is not a human newcomer. `CHANGELOG.md` notes the gate. `docs/architecture.md` records the new dependency of the study crate on the agent crate, which a repository policy test requires.

I did not change `xtask/src/site.rs`, the CLI wiring, the core files, or either fake driver. The reader is recorded under the verifier role, because adding a role variant would ripple through the data crate. The 300-character, 12-item and 40-term limits are my guesses, not tuned values.

Checks: `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` are clean. `cargo test --locked` failed once on the policy test about the undocumented dependency. After the fix I re-ran only the policy test (9 pass), not the whole workspace again. The other suites passed in the earlier run.

checks_run.note: First run failed the xtask policy test because the cap-study to agent dependency was undocumented. I fixed docs/architecture.md. Re-ran the policy test (9 pass) and the other suites (all pass); did not re-run the whole workspace in one command.

open_issues: The gate is not yet called by any publish step. It is a tested library function in athena-cap-study. Wiring it into the real ship path needs a caller that supplies an AgentInvocation template and the rendered HTML. That would touch athena-cli wiring and core, and I judged it a separate change.
xtask/src/site.rs is unchanged. It has no model access, as the reading assumed, and it already rejects uncited and missing data.
Intro text is passed to the gate as an Intro struct (what, walkthrough, glossary), not parsed from intro.json. A loader for intro.json is not written.
The prompt, threshold of 4 and structural limits (300 characters, 12 items, 40 glossary terms) are untuned guesses; the reader is not calibrated against human ratings.
The existing firstmate explainer was not rewritten and not run through the gate (no real model call).
mistakes: The first full cargo test run failed on the architecture dependency policy test, because I added the athena-agent dependency before updating docs/architecture.md. Fixed.
The first design draft of intro_present used an awkward string-prefix dedupe for blank sentences. It works and is tested but is clumsy.
learnings: Role has only Reader, Producer and Verifier. Adding a variant would touch athena-data and many matches, so the newcomer reader is recorded under Role::Verifier.
FakeAgentDriver::new takes a closure over &AgentInvocation, so tests can capture exactly what the reader was given.
xtask/tests/policy.rs fails if a crate dependency edge is missing from docs/architecture.md.
The producer's Bash allows only cargo, chmod, git status/diff/log/show, ls, mv and rm. The Grep and Read tools replace head, tail, rg and wc.
The brief's deliverables list included core, cli and fake files that this design did not need. I did not touch them.
desires: A way to read only the failure lines of cargo test output; the output got truncated.
A listing of what the xtask policy tests enforce, so I could have updated architecture.md up front.
